en.title: Beyond GTA 6: 7 Family-Friendly Open Worlds for Kids
en.summary: With Grand Theft Auto VI on the horizon, parents are wondering what games their kids can play. We've rounded up seven fantastic alternatives that offer open-world fun without the mature content.
en.body:
The colossal hype surrounding **Grand Theft Auto VI** is undeniable, promising hundreds of hours of exploration in Leonida. However, Rockstar's flagship title, with its mature themes of drugs, murder, and sex, is decidedly not for younger players. This leaves a significant demographic – families with children – looking for alternatives that offer similar open-world freedom and engaging gameplay without the adult content. Fortunately, the gaming landscape offers a wealth of fantastic options that capture the spirit of exploration and adventure suitable for all ages.

When seeking a "baby's first GTA," **Lego City Undercover** stands out as a prime candidate. This game mirrors the structure of Rockstar's series with a sprawling open world and a wide array of vehicles to commandeer. Players step into the shoes of police officer Chase McCain, focusing on detective work and crime-solving rather than illicit activities. The game also supports two-player cooperative play, making it a perfect choice for shared family fun, and cleverly weaves in movie references that resonate with adult players.

## Open Worlds for Every Kind of Player

Beyond the Lego universe, several other titles offer compelling open-world experiences tailored for younger audiences. The **Watch Dogs** series, for instance, trades firearms for surveillance cameras and hacking prowess, allowing players to manipulate the city's infrastructure to their advantage. This approach offers a unique take on open-world interaction, where the city itself becomes a playground for creative problem-solving and emergent gameplay. Similarly, **Sleeping Dogs** provides a robust open-world experience with a strong emphasis on engaging hand-to-hand combat, offering a different flavor of urban adventure.

For those who prefer a more laid-back approach, **Animal Crossing: New Horizons** offers a charming escape. Players can build and customize their own island paradise, interacting with a delightful cast of animal neighbors. It's a peaceful, creative sandbox that prioritizes relaxation and personal expression over high-stakes action. For a more structured, yet still incredibly fun experience, **The Skywalker Saga** from the Lego franchise is a monumental achievement, offering vast explorable environments and a staggering roster of characters to collect and play as.

## Games Designed for Shared Fun

When it comes to games that truly bridge the age gap, **Jamboree** shines. This title is particularly adept at accommodating families with a wide range of ages, thanks to its reliance on luck and simple controls. Dice rolls and random events ensure that younger children have a fair chance against older siblings or adults, fostering a truly inclusive environment. The game also includes helpful tutorials for each minigame, making it accessible to everyone.

## What's Next for Family Gaming

While **Grand Theft Auto VI** will undoubtedly dominate headlines, the future of family-friendly gaming is bright. With titles like **Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game**, **Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight**, **Mario Tennis Fever**, **Pokémon Pokopia**, **Rhythm Heaven Groove**, **RollerCoaster Tycoon Classic**, **Star Fox**, and **Yoshi and the Mysterious Book** also on the horizon or readily available, parents have an abundance of choices to keep their kids entertained and engaged in positive gaming experiences.

content_raw: Grand Theft Auto VI is going to be the biggest video game launch of all time, and it's not particularly close. Millions and millions of people are eagerly awaiting their chance to start up the game on Xbox or PlayStation and sink hundreds (or more) hours into Leonida, but there is a very large demographic that Rockstar's game doesn't target: families with kids. GTA 6 is filled with drugs, murder, sex, and pretty much everything else you could think to put in the ESRB rating description for a video game. That means you probably aren't letting your kids play it (seriously, please don't), but there's a good chance they're going to experience some FOMO--especially if they hear other kids at school are playing it (though those kids are probably lying).  So, with that in mind, it's a good idea to have some GTA alternatives ready to go, not only so your kids have something fun to play, but also so you can enjoy a game together. Below are 10 great Grand Theft Auto VI alternatives for kids and families, ranging from games that play like "baby's first GTA" to games that take one element of Rockstar's series and run with it … and one bizarre, family-friendly game that Rockstar happened to make itself.  Lego City Undercover (PS4, Xbox One, Switch, Wii U, PC) Of any game on this list, Lego City Undercover is the one that most resembles Grand Theft Auto in its structure, with access to a big open world and vehicles to drive. Because it's a family-friendly game, however, you play as police officer Chase McCain rather than a hardened criminal, with a particular focus on detective work as you investigate crimes throughout the city. It supports two-person cooperative play, and because there are a whole bunch of movie references intended for parents rather than kids--unless you've shown them Shawshank Redemption already--you may want to pick up the second controller yourself. See at Steam Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight (PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, PC) If you're looking for an open-world alternative to GTA that puts a little more emphasis on combat, then Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a great choice. Mixing the dark, brooding tone you'd expect from Batman with a bunch of the Lego games' silly gags, its structure opens up after the first few hours, letting you glide around the city or speed down the streets in the Batmobile. What really helps it stand out, however, is the combat, which plays like a simplified take on the Arkham games' system that sees Batman effortlessly comboing and countering big groups of goons.
